_doc: Carry weight, item weights, durability, the mount and enchanting (owner 2026-11-23: carry-weight limit from Strength/Constitution, over it you walk slowly, no bag slots; round-1 extras: enchanting and a rideable horse). js/rules/inventory.js is the one reader.

carry._doc: The limit comes from attributes.json (base + Str + Con). Over it: move speed x overloadMove and no sprinting.

weights._doc: Kilograms. Weapons by subtype, armour by Oathwild tier and slot share, jewellery flat.

durability._doc: Every weapon and armour piece starts at `max`. Dying and respawning at a shrine costs `respawnLoss` of each worn piece (owner: 'small durability + gold cost'). At 0 a piece is Broken: it stays on you but gives nothing until repaired. Repair price = repairPerPoint x missing points x item level.

mount._doc: A rideable horse. Calling it takes `summonSeconds` standing still; riding multiplies move speed; taking damage or attacking throws you off; you cannot call it within `combatLock` seconds of a fight.
mount.name: Riding Horse

enchanting._doc: Break (disenchant) a magic or better item to learn one of its enchantments (the item is destroyed). Put a learned enchantment on your own weapon or armour from your Trade skills window, anywhere but in the middle of a fight (owner 2026-11-25: the player does trade skills, not the shrine): its value = a fresh roll for the item's level x (base + Enchanting x perPoint, skills-use.json) and costs gold. Each item takes `slots` of your enchantments (more from the Enchanting perks and the Runic Hand talent).
